common.validationError: Something was wrong with the input. Check the fields and try again.

layer.help: Travel time from your home base. Each layer has its own demands on working arrangement: local can be anything, far has to be (almost) fully remote.

ruleKind.knockoutHelp: If a vacancy has this, it's out. Full stop.
ruleKind.heavy_negativeHelp: Not a knock-out, but it really has to be compensated for.
ruleKind.heavy_positiveHelp: What lifts a vacancy from 'possible' to 'match'.
ruleKind.open_questionHelp: Boundaries you haven't settled yet. An assessment that runs into one should settle it.

vacancies.title: Vacancies
vacancies.empty: No vacancies yet. Add the first one, or import a CSV under Settings.

vacancy.title: Job title
vacancy.sourceHelp: Where you found it: employer's site, LinkedIn, Indeed, a recruiter…
vacancy.sourceVerified: Verified on the employer's own site
vacancy.sourceVerifiedHelp: Aggregators run weeks to months behind. Only once the vacancy is on the employer's own site do you know it's still open.
vacancy.remoteNoteHelp: Hybrid, remote %, 'by agreement'… Exactly what the text says about it.
vacancy.salaryHelp: Leave empty if it isn't stated — that's a signal in itself.
vacancy.verdictReasonHelp: The most important field. Not 'not a great fit', but exactly what clashes and with which rule or preference. This is what feeds the criteria later.
vacancy.doubtsHelp: What you can't tell from the text but that decides it. Also useful if there's an interview.
vacancy.statusNoteHelp: What exactly happened: filled in, sent, reply received, waiting on whom.
vacancy.feedbackIntro: Fill in after the verdict. Was the assessment right? Was the reason off? This is where the correction lands that makes the system sharper — without feedback it learns nothing.
vacancy.feedbackMissed: What was missed or weighed wrongly
vacancy.feedbackInsightHelp: If there's something here, turn it into a rule on the Criteria page, linked to this vacancy.
vacancy.vacancyTextHelp: Pasted in full. Vacancy texts are public, so that's fine.
vacancy.neverDeleted: Vacancies are never deleted. A rejection with its reason is worth more than a match — it's the training data for your criteria. Set the status to Dropped to take it out of the default view.
vacancy.makeRule: Make a rule from this insight
vacancy.rulesFromThis: Rules that came from this vacancy

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.intro: The source of truth for everything that is a boundary. It grows with every verdict and gets sharper — after ten vacancies this isn't a pile of verdicts but a list that lets you see for yourself what's hopeless.
criteria.rationaleHelp: The rejection or conversation that taught this.
criteria.empty: No rules yet. The first one usually comes from the first rejection.
criteria.orderHelp: Knock-outs first, then the conditions per layer, only then the content. That way you don't spend time on a vacancy that fails on the first line.

profile.title: Profile
profile.privacy: No name, address, phone number, email or date of birth. They add nothing to matching — what counts are skills, experience, conditions and preferences. Home town is the only exception: a municipality is enough to judge travel time.
profile.intro: A living document. Every time an application form or interview turns up a detail that wasn't here yet, add it straight away. Better a short profile that's right than a long one with a mistake in it.
profile.requirementsHelp: Hours, language, salary, contract. Location and working-arrangement rules live under Criteria, not here — keeping them in two places goes wrong.
profile.preferencesHelp: What gives energy and what doesn't. Grows with every verdict.
profile.homeBaseHelp: Municipality travel time is judged from.

sources.title: Sources
sources.intro: Where you search, per layer. This is the scan plan you — or an assistant — walk through. Search on employers' own sites where you can; job boards run behind.
sources.label: Name
sources.urlHelp: A search URL with the filters in it is the most useful.
sources.noteHelp: For example: check office days first, or: only if French isn't required.
sources.empty: No sources yet. Start with the local layer: that's the light check you do often.

settings.title: Settings
settings.importHelp: Columns: employer, title, url, source, found_on, layer, verdict, verdict_reason, status, applied_on, closed_on. Extra columns are ignored. Existing vacancies are not overwritten.
settings.importLegacyHelp: Also accepted: the Dutch column names werkgever, titel, bron, datum_gevonden, laag, oordeel, reden_kort, gesolliciteerd, datum_sollicitatie, vervallen_op.
settings.apiEnabled: The API is on. Use the token from API_TOKEN as a Bearer token.
settings.apiDisabled: The API is off. Set API_TOKEN to switch it on.
settings.apiHelp: An assistant such as Claude Code can add and assess vacancies and read the criteria through the MCP server. See the README for how to connect it.
settings.passwordChanged: Password changed. All other sessions have been logged out.
settings.passwordShort: The new password is too short.
settings.import_toolarge: The file is larger than 10 MB.

login.title: Log in
login.rate: Too many attempts. Try again in fifteen minutes.

setup.intro: First time here? Create the account you'll log in with. There's one account; the password is stored hashed.
setup.usernameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash. 3–32 characters.
setup.passwordHelp: At least {n} characters. A sentence works better than a word.
